compatibility.coordinate_policy: Never infer or fabricate coordinates. Existing weather-map markers are retained as legacy unverified values until independently checked.
compatibility.revision_history: Git commit history; per-record revision fields reserved.

notes: This is an initial evidence-backed data structure, not a completed suitability model.
No activity scores are assigned in this dataset.
Historical water-quality results are not current safety advice.
Operator meeting points are not treated as official universal departure terminals.

DENR-EMB 2022 monitoring-station coordinates and fecal-coliform summaries are recorded separately from beach-centroid coordinates; they must not be used as beach centroids or current bathing-water advice.
Hagdan Beach remains a provisional identity: TPB map labels Sitio Hagdan but does not list Hagdan Beach in its Beach / Dive Site index; a secondary guide uses the beach name.
TPB tourist map also lists Lugutan Beach, which is outside the fixed 13-beach scope and is not silently added to the dataset.
White Beach historical monitoring is represented by Boat Stations 1–3 as spatially distinct DENR-EMB sampling points, not by a single whole-beach measurement.
The 2022 DENR-EMB report also provides quarterly oil-and-grease results (April, June, September and November) for the nine recorded sampling stations. These remain historical, station-specific data.

White Beach now includes a peer-reviewed October 2022 sediment and benthic-macrofauna study for Stations 1–3. These are station-specific research observations, not a whole-beach or current-condition assessment.
Sediment-study coordinates are stored separately from beach-centroid coordinates and must not be used as public beach markers.
Bulabog Beach water-quality record is linked to the Ralph's Place ambient station using the explicit station-name alias in the DENR-EMB 2021 regional report; 2022 results remain station-specific.
Lapuz-Lapuz has a historical DENR-EMB station coordinate from the 2021 report; this is not a beach-centroid coordinate and no matching 2022 annual result is asserted.

DENR-EMB 2021 report contains separate 2006–2019 and 2020-onwards station inventories. Lapuz-Lapuz is found only in the older table; the current Bulabog station is the 2020-onwards Ralph's Place record. Distinct historical points are not merged.

Balinghai, Banyugan and Punta Bunga legacy markers exactly match their Mapcarta-displayed OSM natural=beach feature coordinates. Secondary guide points are within ~12 m and ~9 m for Balinghai and Banyugan, but ~103 m away for Punta Bunga; all remain feature-reference points, not surveyed centroids.
Access claims for Balinghai and Punta Bunga are conflicting or provisional; the dataset does not assert definitive current public access.

Coordinate audit now cross-checks Diniwid, Tulubhan, Tambisaan, Ilig-Iligan, Puka and White Beach against Mapcarta-displayed OSM natural=beach features and DENR-EMB station coordinates. Matches and discrepancies are explicitly retained; no beach-centroid coordinates are promoted.

Secondary guide GPS points from Lakad Pilipinas 2023 have been added as separate reference coordinates for 11 named beaches. They are not substituted for legacy markers or DENR monitoring-station coordinates; all three point types remain distinct.

For Puka and Ilig-Iligan, legacy markers match the travel-guide point but are displaced from OSM beach-feature and DENR station points. For White Beach, the legacy marker is exactly Boat Station 2. These are unresolved map-point identity differences, not reasons to overwrite coordinates.

Hagdan and Lapuz-Lapuz now carry OSM locality reference points only. These are neighborhood coordinates, not beach feature or centroid coordinates; Hagdan Beach remains a provisional separate beach identity.

Added station-specific CY 2023 Boracay coastline monitoring results from the official DENR-EMB Region VI 2023 Regional State of the Brown Environment Report (SRC-024): fecal-coliform geomeans and compliance, dissolved-oxygen averages and compliance, and total-suspended-solids averages where unambiguous. Historical station values are not beach-wide or current real-time bathing-water assessments.

For the 2023 fecal-coliform compliance chart, the caption specifies Jan–Nov 2023 while report narrative refers to 12 sampling events; event counts are omitted pending clarification. Ralph's Place TSS is excluded because the report contains conflicting 2023 values (32.3 and 33.4 mg/L).

The 2023 report identifies Diniwid Beach and Tulubhan as Class SB stations with multiple individual fecal-coliform sampling events above the 100 MPN/100 ml guideline, despite annual geomeans below 100; annual mean compliance must not be interpreted as every sampling event being compliant.

Added SRC-025, the official 2024 Regional State of the Brown Environment Report. It confirms a January–July 2024 Boracay water-quality data section, but its PDF could not be retrieved for full station-table validation; no numeric station values were ingested.

SRC-026 reports an EMB statement that all 24 Boracay monitoring stations passed water-safety tests in January–June 2024. This is historical island-level context only; it contains no station-specific numeric values and does not establish current beach-specific bathing-water safety.

SRC-027 reports March 2026 in-situ screening at four Boracay outfalls: DO, temperature and pH were compliant, while laboratory results for TSS, color and fecal coliform were pending at publication. Outfall measurements are not beach bathing-water results and are not used to infer any beach's current safety.

Added the Boracay-specific 25+5 m easement and the national public-use shoreline easement legal framework (SRC-028 to SRC-031). These are distinct legal concepts. The public-use easement does not establish a practical public approach route or current access conditions at any individual beach; all beach-specific access statuses remain unchanged.

Added the 2020 BMDAI/BIWC marine ecological survey for Sitio Bolabog to the Bulabog passport as station-specific evidence (SRC-003). Coral cover at A1 and seagrass cover at T1–T3 are not extrapolated to the entire beach. T1's printed coordinate is preserved as an anomaly and excluded from mapping; the Sitio Malabunot A2 station is not assigned to any target beach.

The 2020 EPRMP marine survey reports eight seagrass species in its narrative, while the station table lists ten taxon rows and inconsistent station totals. Species composition is not normalized pending source reconciliation.

Added island-wide marine resource mapping sources SRC-032 to SRC-035. The 2020 assessment records approximately 763 ha coral reefs, 95.37 ha seagrass and 1.90 ha mangroves; the 2026 report of 2024–2025 DENR PENRO validation records 763.30 ha coral habitat on Boracay. These are different reporting vintages and island-level habitat extents, not beach-level live coral cover or reef-condition scores.

The 2020 DENR/secondary mapping sources report nine seagrass species and barangay-level cover estimates (Balabag 81.84%, Manocmanoc 53.85%, Yapak 53.68%). The underlying mapping report was described as subject to regional review; no values are assigned to individual beaches.

The DENR 2020 Annual Report confirms that marine resource and MPA mapping/delineation results were presented to stakeholders, but the reviewed source does not provide legal designation instruments or boundary coordinates. PAIS Aklan query did not surface a Boracay-specific protected-area record; because PAIS data are encoded and subject to ongoing validation, the legal MPA/protected-area status remains unverified, not negative.

Corrected a provenance defect in White Beach and Bulabog hydrodynamics: Amihan/Habagat exposure fields previously marked supported without sources are now provisional and cite the coarse coast-side map plus PAGASA's national monsoon-direction reference (SRC-001, SRC-038). These are directional inferences only; local wind, waves, currents and rip-current behaviour remain unknown.

Registered NAMRIA primary hydrographic data pathways (SRC-039 to SRC-041): bathymetry chart/data ASCII XYZ, georeferenced nautical charts, and station/time-specific tidal-current and wave data can be requested. No numerical hydrographic values have been ingested.

NAMRIA Notices to Mariners 2026-04 records a submarine pipeline correction for charts 1544 and 4358. Chart 1544 and chart 4358 use separate coordinate pairs in the notice; these representations must not be merged. A navigation-chart correction is not treated as a beach-specific hazard or exclusion zone.

The NAMRIA ENC availability list dated 13 February 2025 includes PH5CATIC (Port of Caticlan) and PH2CVZ40 (Central Visayas), both affected by the 2026 pipeline correction. Availability confirms potential chart coverage only, not extraction of bathymetric data.

Added approximate published shoreline lengths: White Beach ~4.0 km (DENR-EMB 2022 report and 2024 peer-reviewed paper) and Bulabog ~2.5 km (2024 peer-reviewed paper), SRC-002 and SRC-042. These approximate lengths do not establish surveyed boundaries or centroids.

Bulabog reef and seagrass presence are now recorded as supported historical presence based on the 2024 peer-reviewed paper and the 2020 local marine survey (SRC-042, SRC-003). Reef boundaries, reef crest, current condition, bathymetry and current seagrass extent remain unknown.

Added historical 2011–2012 total-coliform and stable-isotope study context to White Beach Site 3 near Station 2 and Bulabog Sites 5–7 (SRC-042). The study is pre-2018 rehabilitation, measures total coliform rather than fecal coliform, and does not provide verified GPS coordinates for the sites. Its 80–94% isotope-mixing estimate applies collectively to Sites 3, 6 and 7, not to either beach individually.

The 2012 study describes historical wastewater discharge points in the Bulabog area and a canal near White Beach Site 3. The article also states that illegal pipes were uncovered and permanently sealed during the 2018 rehabilitation; no claim is made that the historical discharge arrangement persists today.

Added qualitative seasonal and surface-current context from SRC-042 to White Beach and Bulabog. White Beach is described as leeward/calm during summer with somewhat stronger waves during Habagat; Bulabog is described as windward during summer. The paper also describes weak surface current on the west side and eastward current along the east side. These are historical island/side-level descriptions, not measured local wave or current series.

SRC-042 Site 10 is described only as a northern Yapak site facing Carabao Island with rougher waves. No exact beach name or GPS coordinate is provided, so Site 10 is not assigned to Puka Beach, Ilig-Iligan Beach or another target beach.

Added qualitative sediment-core trace-element anomalies from the 2012 study (SRC-042): chromium at White Beach Site 1 near Station 0, lead at White Beach Site 4 near Station 3, chromium at Bulabog Site 5 and zinc at Bulabog Site 6. No numeric concentrations or definitive pollution-source attribution are assigned; all observations predate the 2018 rehabilitation.

Added CY 2022 station-level annual averages and event-compliance data for dissolved oxygen, total suspended solids, water temperature, phosphate as phosphorus and nitrate to 10 target stations (SRC-002). Each result preserves the 12 monthly primary-parameter sampling events. Oil & Grease remains in its separate four-quarter dataset.

CY 2022 pH annual averages were transcribed for the same 10 stations, but pH guideline/compliance was not normalized because the report's narrative and figure captions disagree on Class SB/SC pH ranges.

At Puka Beach, DENR reported 75% TSS compliance across 12 sampling events and attributed elevated suspended solids at northern stations partly to strong waves and currents. This is a station-specific historical interpretation, not a measured wave-climate dataset.

Coordinate audit against the 2022 DENR-EMB Annual Water Quality Assessment Report confirms that the 10 active station coordinates in the beach passports match the report's DMS table after conversion. Exact source DMS strings are now retained alongside decimal coordinates.

Ralph's Place has two distinct DENR station references: 2021 RSoBER Table 4.54 at 11°58′09.0″N, 121°55′38.4″E and 2022 Annual Assessment Report at 11°58′09.9″N, 121°55′39.3″E. The points are 38.9 m apart. The 2022 point remains the active station coordinate; the 2021 point is retained as a historical reference. Neither is a beach centroid.

Cross-check against 2023 RSoBER Table 4.50 confirms that all 10 target monitoring stations retain the same names, water-body classes and DMS coordinates as the 2022 DENR-EMB Annual Water Quality Assessment Report. Station coordinate records now cite both SRC-002 and SRC-024 with coordinate_source_years [2022, 2023].

Ralph's Place remains a documented exception across report vintages: 2021 RSoBER Table 4.54 coordinate differs by 38.9 m from the identical 2022 and 2023 station coordinates. The 2021 point remains a separate historical station reference.

Added CY 2023 phosphate-as-phosphorus and nitrate annual averages plus event-compliance data for the same 10 target stations (SRC-024). Phosphate WQGV is 0.2 mg P/L; nitrate WQGV is 10 mg/L. All 10 target stations were reported 100% compliant in all 12 sampling events for both parameters.

CY 2023 primary-parameter sampling count is retained as 12 from the report narrative. The fecal-coliform compliance figure caption says Jan–Nov 2023; this internal date-span discrepancy remains explicitly documented.

Added 2024 WQMA-level context: Manila Bulletin reports that all 24 Boracay monitoring stations passed the Jan–Jun 2024 water-safety test (SRC-044); the official DEPDev 2024 report lists Boracay among three WQMAs meeting fecal-coliform guideline values and reports pH/nitrate compliance across all 40 WQMAs (SRC-045). Neither source provides station-level numeric values, so no 2024 figures were assigned to individual beach stations.

Added EMB-6/BIWQMACA outfall sampling from 2–3 March 2026 (SRC-043). Bulabog Outfall 1 and Bulabog Drainage Outfall are recorded as separate outfall points in the Bulabog area; Malabunot Outfall 2 and Lugutan Outfall remain unassigned to target beaches. On-site DO, temperature and pH were reported compliant at all four outfalls; TSS, color and fecal-coliform laboratory results were pending at publication. This is not ambient beach bathing-water evidence.

The 2024 RSoBER PDF remains inaccessible for station-table extraction. The official WQMA page currently links the Boracay Annual Assessment Report 2022; 2024 station-level values remain an explicit data gap.

Added Panay News cross-check SRC-046 for the 2–3 March 2026 outfall monitoring. It conflicts with Daily Tribune on temperature: Daily Tribune reports DO, temperature and pH compliant at all four sites; Panay News reports elevated temperature at some sites while DO and pH complied. Temperature status is therefore unconfirmed; no numerical values or affected outfall names are published. DO and pH remain reported compliant, not numerically validated.

Added DENR Administrative Order No. 2019-15 (SRC-047), which designates Boracay Island as a Water Quality Management and Conservation Area (WQMACA) and describes boundary-control-point segments explicitly referencing Ilig-Iligan, Lapuz-Lapuz, Bulabog, Tulubhan, Tambisaan, White/Long Beach, Diniwid, Punta Bunga and Banyugan. These control points define the WQMACA perimeter, not beach boundaries or beach centroids. WQMACA is not treated as proof of a separate NIPAS protected area or site-specific MPA.

Added the Coral Triangle Atlas registry record for Boracay Island Tourist Zone Marine Reserve (SRC-048) as an unverified candidate MPA record only. The registry supplies no legal/formal instrument, no area and no boundary polygon; it is not used to assert MPA status for any target beach or to assign its reference coordinate to a beach.

All 13 beach passports now distinguish the confirmed island-wide WQMACA designation from the still-unverified site-specific NIPAS/MPA status. Nine passports carry locality references explicitly named in the DENR order; the remaining four retain island-wide context without a fabricated local boundary intersection.

Corrected the site-wide protected-area research conclusion after locating the primary legal instrument: Presidential Proclamation No. 1801 (SRC-049) expressly declares Boracay Islands, Aklan as a tourist zone and marine reserve under the Philippine Tourism Authority. All 13 passports now record this supported island-level designation. The proclamation does not provide beach-specific marine boundaries, coordinates, zoning or no-take limits; no such geometry is inferred.

Added the Supreme Court decision in G.R. Nos. 167707 and 173775 (SRC-050) to clarify the legal distinction between Proclamation No. 1801's tourism/ecological administration purpose and land classification under Proclamation No. 1064. The Court's discussion of the lack of specific limits for land classification is not interpreted as invalidating the marine-reserve designation.

Updated the Coral Triangle Atlas record SRC-048: its missing legal-instrument field is now cross-referenced to the primary Proclamation No. 1801 source SRC-049. The Atlas point remains unsuitable for delineating protected-area or beach boundaries.

Added the Philippine Coast Guard 2019 National Oil Spill Contingency Plan Annex 10 (SRC-051), which lists Boracay Island TZMR as a national marine protected area with year 1978 and a single reference coordinate. This independently corroborates the Proclamation No. 1801 island-level marine-reserve designation but provides no boundary polygon, area, zoning or beach-level limits. The annex heading referring to NIPAS is not used to claim that the 1978 designation was originally established under the later NIPAS statute.
